thread.title: Brace for another nose-dive for stocks — and welcome it - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Brace for another nose-dive for stocks — and welcome it - MarketWatch
text:
In what would last week have seemed like a Wall Street miracle, stocks are hard at work on their fifth up day in a row this morning.
The Teflon equity market we’ve known and loved resurfaced yesterday as it marched onward and upward, past inflation data and a pop higher in the 10-year Treasury yield nearer the 3% line in the sand. The VIX VIX, -0.67% is under 20.
The only problem is that it all looks a little too easy, like a “Scooby-Doo” mystery that’s all squared away in mere minutes. Ruh-roh?
At this rates.. the 10 year will break 3% this week. I honestly have no idea how ANYONE could be bullish SPX other than the standard chaser... ( it went up 2 days.. its bullish...or it went down 2 days I am bearish ) nonsense..
— Bama (@Bamabroker) February 15, 2018 There are some doubts that equities can just sail on upward from here, end of story. Among them is our call of the day , which comes from CFRA’s chief investment strategist Sam Stovall, who says the S&P 500 “will likely have to retest its recent low.”
That low came last Thursday, when the S&P careened down to 2,532.69 before snapping back. As Stovall and others have pointed out, the index didn’t break its 200-day moving average, which helped it then slingshot upward more than 6% over the next four trading days.
However, the reason a retest can’t be avoided is “recoveries from sharp selloffs require reassurances,” the CFRA strategist says. In other words, investors will need proof that the bounce was for real.
The good news? That pullback will “present a second buying opportunity, rather than usher in a new bear market, since we don’t see recession on the horizon,” says Stovall.
Arbeter Investments A similar view comes from technical analyst Mark Arbeter, who says there’s more than a “50/50 chance we rollover and test (within 1% to 2%) the recent lows.”
A V-shaped bottom is unlikely, “as there was a fair amount of technical damage to a lot of stocks,” the Arbeter Investments president tells clients.
Key market gauges The Dow DJIA, +1.23% is cruising above 25,000 for the first time in two weeks, while the S&P SPX, +1.21% and Nasdaq COMP, +1.58% are also climbing. Asian stocks matched Wall Street’s prior ride higher with strong gains in Hong Kong and Japan , though several markets there are closed for the Lunar New Year holiday. European stocks SXXP, +0.53% are also charging higher.
The dollar DXY, -0.45% is getting mugged again, crude CLH8, +1.30% is up a bit, but pared back an earlier stronger bump . Gold GCJ8, -0.14% is flat. The yield on the 10-year Treasury TMUBMUSD10Y, -0.03% is right at 2.923%.
See the Market Snapshot column for the latest action, and check out why the U.S. dollar isn’t getting any love .
Bitcoin BTCUSD, +6.64% — or “noxious poison,” as Charlie Munger calls it — is taking aim at $10,000.
The chart It’s been quite a ride down for the dollar USDJPY, -0.80% against the yen recently, and it looks like the same is on tap for Thursday. Our chart of the day comes from London Capital Group’s head of research, Jasper Lawler, whose chart below shows how the yen has broken out of its long-term trading range to hit a 15-month high recently.
“The current bout of dollar weakness could still stumble, particularly as EURUSD and GBPUSD approach multi-year peaks at 1.25 and 1.43 respectively. But the breakout in the yen skews the risks in favour of another leg lower in the buck,” says Lawler.
London Capital Group The buzz Cisco CSCO, +4.73% is cruising higher on signs it has turned a corner . It’s hovering at post-2000 highs in premarket after its earnings and outlook topped estimates.
Read: Cisco is ‘putting together newer growth engines’ — analysts react to earnings
TripAdvisor TRIP, +4.13% is soaring after a bullish forecast .
Applied Materials AMAT, +3.91% is up a bit on a dividend rise and earnings beat .
Avon AVP, +13.22% is up after results, and Shake Shack SHAK, +3.96% is coming after the close. As well, Kraft Heinz KHC, +1.10% is due to release a post-merger update after the bell.
It’s 13-F time, which means investors can peek inside the portfolios of big institutional managers, though the info is from the fourth quarter. Sometimes shares mentioned react. Among the highlights, Warren Buffett’s Berkshire Hathaway BRK.A, +1.66% BRK.B, +1.68% added Apple AAPL, +3.36% and Teva shares TEVA, +7.66% and cut a stake in IBM IBM, +0.81% .
David Tepper’s Appaloosa Management upped exposure to Micron MU, +0.12% , Facebook FB, +0.25% , Apple and Bank of America BAC, +0.66% , and made bets on Caesars CZR, +2.73% and MGM, +1.63% .
David Einhorn’s Greenlight Capital added to a Brighthouse BHF, +0.66% stake and took a small Twitter TWTR, -0.41% position.
Pretty much every major 13F filing thus far: buy either $GOOG , $TWX , or $MSFT . The end.
— Market Folly (@marketfolly) February 14, 2018 Amazon AMZN, +0.74% and Bank of America BAC, +0.66% may be teaming up on lending, says report .
Healthier Happy Meals? McDonald’s MCD, +0.49% sets that as a worldwide goal for 2022 .
The economy Data out so far have shown jobless claims edging up , while inflation components of the Empire State and Philly Fed indexes vaulted higher in February . Industrial output ended a streak of gains . Still to come, a home-builder index.
The stat Everytown School shootings in the U.S. since 2013. 18 — That’s how many school shootings the U.S. has suffered so far in 2018, according to Everytown for Gun Safety .
The death toll from Wednesday’s gun attack at Florida’s Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Broward County, Fla., stands at 17, with many more injured. Everytown’s map above shows the locations of the 290 school shootings since 2013, as of Feb. 8.
